answer: Policies are written in ridge, settled in gale, and lantern lists every payout. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 34% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 151 aliases cost 377 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
